`call_tool` opens the local `repo_path`, and `git_diff_unstaged` returns `repo.git.diff(...)` for unstaged working-tree changes. The diff can contain non-public local file contents. Diff text, paths, and hunks can also be authored by contributors to third-party or multi-writer repository content.

`call_tool` opens the local `repo_path`, and `git_diff_staged` returns `repo.git.diff(..., "--cached")` for staged changes. The diff can expose non-public staged file contents. Diff text, paths, and hunks can also be contributor-authored in third-party or multi-writer repository content.

`call_tool` opens the local `repo_path`, and `git_diff` validates `target` then returns `repo.git.diff(...)` against that revision. The diff can expose non-public repository contents. `git_commit` writes a new local commit with the supplied `message` via `repo.index.commit(message)` and returns only the resulting commit hash. The code does not send data to an attacker-readable destination and does not return repository contents.

`git_add` stages selected local repository paths using `repo.git.add`. It changes only local repository index state and returns a fixed success string, with no repository contents or attacker-readable delivery shown in the code.

`git_reset` calls `repo.index.reset()` to unstage local changes and returns a fixed string. The code changes local repository state but does not return secrets, untrusted repository text, or send data to an attacker-readable destination.

`git_log` reads local commit history from `repo.git.log(...)` or `repo.iter_commits(...)` and returns hashes, authors, dates, and messages. This can reveal non-public local repository history. Commit authors and messages can be authored by outside contributors in third-party/multi-writer repositorie

`git_create_branch` writes a local branch and returns the new `branch_name` and `base.name`; if `base_branch` is omitted, `base` is `repo.active_branch`, so the response can reveal local repository branch metadata. Branch/ref names can also be attacker-authored in third-party or multi-writer reposit

`git_checkout` validates and checks out the supplied `branch_name`, changing local repository working-tree/HEAD state, and returns only the supplied branch name in a success string. The code does not return repository contents or send data to an attacker-readable destination.

`git_show` reads a local commit selected by `revision` and returns commit hash, author, date, message, file paths, and patch contents. `git_branch` runs `repo.git.branch(...)` and returns branch information from the local repository. This can reveal non-public local branch/ref names. Branch names can also be attacker-authored when listing remote/all branches from third-party or multi-writer repositories.
